games.why: Yes, this happened. On 15 October astronomers at the University of Warwick in England said a dead star called a white dwarf would look green if we could see it. Stars normally look white, yellow, red or blue, because their colour mostly depends on how hot they are, so a green star was thought impossible. This one has swallowed rocky debris from its own planets, and sodium from that debris soaks up the orange part of its light, leaving a green glow. Nobody has actually seen it with their own eyes: the team worked out its colour from its light, using a model of how human vision works.
